rationale: Browser-capture native lowering orders each sibling list by where its ink lands: a node that paints nothing, takes no input, and does not clip, composite as a group or transform is drawn at the earliest position its subtree draws, which is pixel-identical to Chrome's paint order. The overlapping-reorder audit that decides the flat fallback now counts a pair only when both nodes paint or either takes input, and counts SVG shapes and per-side borders as ink. The flat fallback is kept. The DesignIR contract is unchanged; captured trees keep their hierarchy more often. A new lens-calibration fixture (22-local-flatten) is added. Chromium stays the only oracle and Skia/Dawn the renderer; no design-import, Chromium, rendering, or packaging authority moves.
